adjudication_records.issue_text: app/controllers/topics_controller.rb:98 — State-changing unsubscribe is a plain GET with no CSRF token/signed key (contrast DigestUnsubscribeKey), so any cross-site ``, forum-post link, or logged-in browser prefetch silently mutes a victim's topic.

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds `get "t/:slug/:topic_id/unsubscribe" => "topics#unsubscribe"` and `get "t/:topic_id/unsubscribe" => "topics#unsubscribe"` routes, and implements `TopicsController#unsubscribe` which mutates `TopicUser.notification_level` and saves (`tu.save!`) on a plain GET request. Since Rails’ CSRF protections generally don’t apply to GET, and the diff shows no signed token/key validation for this endpoint, it is vulnerable to cross-site request triggering (e.g., an `` or prefetch) that silently changes a logged-in user’s notification state for a topic.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/controllers/topics_controller.rb:105 — TopicUser.find_by` can return nil (any logged-in user hitting the URL for a topic they never visited, or a row deleted after the email) and `tu.notification_level` then raises NoMethodError -> 500.

adjudication_records.primary_judge_reasoning: Both point out the same underlying bug: TopicUser.find_by may return nil when no record exists, and subsequent calls on `tu` (e.g., `tu.notification_level`) will raise a NoMethodError (nil dereference).

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/controllers/topics_controller.rb:107 — Toggle is not idempotent: tracking/watching -> regular on first click (user still gets reply/mention emails) then -> muted on reload, so the page claims "you will stop receiving notifications" after a click that only set `regular`.

adjudication.rationale: In `TopicsController#unsubscribe`, the action explicitly *toggles* `TopicUser#notification_level`: if `tu.notification_level > :regular` it sets it to `:regular`, otherwise it sets it to `:muted` (new method starting at `def unsubscribe`). That makes the endpoint non-idempotent and means a user coming from `tracking`/`watching` will land on `regular` after the first click, while the Ember template (`topic/unsubscribe.hbs`) always shows `topic.unsubscribe.stop_notifications` (“You will stop receiving notifications...”), which is inconsistent with the actual state set on first click. Reloading/hitting the link again would then flip to `muted`, matching the complaint.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/controllers/topics_controller.rb:8 — ensure_logged_in` on an emailed GET link means a recipient without a browser session (typical on mobile mail clients) gets Discourse's not-logged-in 404/403 page with no login redirect or return_to, so the unsubscribe silently never happens.

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds an emailed "stop receiving notifications about this particular topic" link via `unsubscribe_url: post.topic.unsubscribe_url` and locale `unsubscribe_link` pointing to `/t/:topic_id/unsubscribe`. That route maps to `TopicsController#unsubscribe`, which mutates `TopicUser` based on `current_user` (`TopicView.new(..., current_user)`, `TopicUser.find_by(user_id: current_user.id, ...)`) and has no anonymous/sessionless fallback or token-based auth. If the recipient clicks from an email client without an existing Discourse session, the action cannot determine the user and will fail/deny rather than perform the unsubscribe. The specific claim about the exact 404/403 page/redirect behavior depends on `ensure_logged_in` implementation not shown here, but the underlying broken behavior (email link requiring a logged-in session) is directly implied by this diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/assets/javascripts/discourse/routes/topic-unsubscribe.js.es6:4 — Ember route only calls `loadTopicView` (never the server unsubscribe endpoint), so any in-app navigation to `/t/:slug/:id/unsubscribe` (pasted link in a post, back/forward, `Discourse.URL.routeTo`) renders "You will stop receiving notifications" without changing anything.

adjudication.rationale: The new Ember route `app/assets/javascripts/discourse/routes/topic-unsubscribe.js.es6` defines `model(params)` that only does `PostStream.loadTopicView(params.id)` and never calls the new server-side `TopicsController#unsubscribe` endpoint (wired at `get .../unsubscribe => topics#unsubscribe`). Therefore, if the SPA handles navigation to `/t/:slug/:id/unsubscribe` client-side (no full page reload), it will render the unsubscribe UI/text without performing the notification-level toggle implemented in `TopicsController#unsubscribe`.

adjudication_records.issue_text: lib/email/message_builder.rb:67 — unsubscribe_link` locale now hard-requires `%{unsubscribe_url}`; any other/plugin caller passing `add_unsubscribe_link: true` without it raises I18n::MissingInterpolationArgument (or renders the literal placeholder) and kills that email job - the spec had to be patched to hide this.

adjudication.rationale: The diff changes `config/locales/server.en.yml` `unsubscribe_link` to include `%{unsubscribe_url}`. In `lib/email/message_builder.rb#html_part`, when `@opts[:add_unsubscribe_link]` is true it calls `I18n.t('unsubscribe_link', template_args)` with whatever was merged into `@template_args`; there is no default for `unsubscribe_url`. Therefore any call site that sets `add_unsubscribe_link: true` but does not pass `unsubscribe_url` will trigger `I18n::MissingInterpolationArgument` (or leave an unresolved placeholder, depending on I18n settings) and break email rendering. The spec was updated to pass `unsubscribe_url`, which further indicates this new requirement.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/controllers/topics_controller.rb:111 — tu.save!` bypasses `TopicUser.change`: no `notifications_changed_at`/`notifications_reason_id=user_changed` and no MessageBus `notification_level_change` publish, so open topic tabs keep the stale level and the reason text stays wrong.

adjudication.rationale: In the new `TopicsController#unsubscribe`, the code directly mutates and `tu.save!`s a `TopicUser` record instead of using `TopicUser.change(...)` (see `app/models/topic_user.rb`), which is the path that publishes `MessageBus` `/topic/#{topic_id}` `notification_level_change` events. Since this action is explicitly toggling `notification_level`, bypassing that mechanism means other open clients/tabs won’t receive the live update and can display a stale notification level until refresh. The finding’s extra claims about `notifications_changed_at`/`notification_reason_id` aren’t verifiable from this diff, but the missing `TopicUser.change` side effects (at least the MessageBus publish) are directly supported by the shown changes.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/controllers/topics_controller.rb:105 — Read-modify-write toggle is non-atomic and unguarded; concurrent double-clicks or a concurrent `TopicUser.change` from the mailer (`last_emailed_post_number`) can interleave and land on an unintended level.

adjudication.rationale: The new `TopicsController#unsubscribe` action performs a read-modify-write on `TopicUser` (`tu = TopicUser.find_by(...)`; branch on `tu.notification_level`; then `tu.save!`) without any locking or atomic update. Two concurrent requests (e.g., double-clicking the unsubscribe link) can both read the same starting `notification_level` (e.g., `tracking`) and both write the same result (`regular`), so the net effect can differ from the user’s intended toggle sequence. The finding’s specific claim about interleaving with `TopicUser.change(... last_emailed_post_number ...)` is less directly supported because `save!` will typically only update dirty columns, but the core non-atomic toggle race is real and introduced by this diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/controllers/topics_controller.rb:102 — Slug mismatch returns a browser-cacheable 301 to `unsubscribe_url`; combined with the mutating GET this means a bookmarked/old-slug link keeps auto-firing the mutation on every visit and 301 fires before any check that the user has a TopicUser row.

adjudication.rationale: In `TopicsController#unsubscribe`, the action is reached via `get "t/:slug/:topic_id/unsubscribe"` and it mutates state (toggles `TopicUser.notification_level` and `tu.save!`) on a GET. The slug-mismatch branch returns a permanent redirect (`redirect_to @topic_view.topic.unsubscribe_url, status: 301`) before any `TopicUser` lookup, so an old-slug URL can be cached by the browser as a 301 to the canonical `/unsubscribe` URL; subsequent visits to the old URL can be transparently redirected to the mutating GET, effectively re-triggering the toggle on each visit. Also, the action assumes `TopicUser.find_by(...)` returns a row (no nil-check), so the redirect occurring before that lookup matches the finding’s ordering concern.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/assets/javascripts/discourse/routes/topic-unsubscribe.js.es6:3 — Route uses `params.id` while the server route param is `:topic_id`, and there is no `PreloadStore`-consistency guarantee: if `loadTopicView` refetches after the mutation the button shows the mutated level while the copy above it still says notifications are stopped even when level is `regular`.

adjudication.rationale: The Ember route is defined in `app-route-map.js.es6` as `/t/:slug/:id/unsubscribe`, so using `params.id` in `app/assets/javascripts/discourse/routes/topic-unsubscribe.js.es6` is consistent with the client-side URL param naming. The server-side Rails route uses `:topic_id` for the same path segment, but that does not make the client route incorrect (Ember reads from its own route definition, not Rails’ param key). Also, the template text `stopNotificiationsText` only interpolates `model.fancyTitle` and does not depend on notification level, so the claimed UI inconsistency (“copy above it still says notifications are stopped even when level is regular”) is not verifiable from this diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: config/locales/server.en.yml:1852 — Locale changed to a YAML block scalar with a trailing newline and a bare "click here" link; the text-part body (`message_builder.rb:90`) now contains an extra blank line and the link text gives no URL context for plaintext readers.

adjudication.rationale:
The diff does change `unsubscribe_link` in `config/locales/server.en.yml` to a YAML block scalar (`|`) with an intentional blank line between two paragraphs, so the rendered string will include an extra newline. However, the finding’s claim about the *text-part* body in `message_builder.rb:90` is not verifiable from this diff: the only shown logic is `html_part`, which cooks the markdown to HTML and substitutes `%{unsubscribe_link}`. Also, whether “click here” lacks URL context for plaintext readers depends on how the plaintext part is generated (not shown here); the translation still contains the URL as markdown `[%{unsubscribe_url}]`.
Overall this reads as an unverified/subjective UX nit rather than a concrete, diff-provable defect.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/controllers/topics_controller.rb:113 — perform_show_response` for the unsubscribe action skips `discourse_expires_in`, `canonical_url`, `track_visit_to_topic` and `X-Robots-Tag` handling that `show` applies, so the page is served with inconsistent caching/SEO headers.

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds a new `unsubscribe` action in `TopicsController` that directly builds `@topic_view`, mutates `TopicUser`, then calls `perform_show_response` without going through `show`’s code path. From the diff alone we can verify that any logic implemented specifically inside `show` (as opposed to inside `perform_show_response`) will not run for `unsubscribe`, so it’s reasonable to flag potential inconsistencies in caching/SEO/visit-tracking if those are handled in `show`. However, the diff does not show what `show` does beyond the snippet, nor what `perform_show_response` includes, so the specific claim about skipping `discourse_expires_in`, `canonical_url`, `track_visit_to_topic`, and `X-Robots-Tag` cannot be conclusively verified here.

adjudication_records.issue_text: config/locales/server.en.yml:1852 — Shared `unsubscribe_link` string now interpolates `%{unsubscribe_url}`, so any MessageBuilder caller (plugins/other mailers) passing `add_unsubscribe_link: true` without `unsubscribe_url` raises I18n::MissingInterpolationArgument in both body and html_part (the spec had to be changed to keep passing, confirming the contract break).

adjudication.rationale: The diff changes `config/locales/server.en.yml` `unsubscribe_link` to include `%{unsubscribe_url}` but `Email::MessageBuilder#html_part` still does `I18n.t('unsubscribe_link', template_args)` whenever `@opts[:add_unsubscribe_link]` is true, without providing a default `unsubscribe_url`. The spec had to be updated to pass `unsubscribe_url`, confirming that callers using only `add_unsubscribe_link: true` would now raise `I18n::MissingInterpolationArgument` unless they also provide `unsubscribe_url`. This is a backward-incompatible behavioral break introduced by the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: lib/email/message_builder.rb:24 — template_args` provides no default/fallback for `unsubscribe_url` and `unsubscribe_link` is rendered unconditionally when `add_unsubscribe_link` is set; the builder should default it or omit the per-topic sentence when absent instead of pushing a new required arg onto every caller.

adjudication.rationale: In lib/email/message_builder.rb, when `@opts[:add_unsubscribe_link]` is true it unconditionally renders `I18n.t('unsubscribe_link', template_args)`. The diff changes `config/locales/server.en.yml` `unsubscribe_link` to include `%{unsubscribe_url}`, but `@template_args` in MessageBuilder’s initializer has no default `unsubscribe_url` (only site_name/base_url/user_preferences_url). This effectively makes `unsubscribe_url` a required option for every caller that sets `add_unsubscribe_link`, unless all such callers pass it. The diff updates one caller (app/mailers/user_notifications.rb) and the spec, but the diff alone can’t prove there are no other callers, so it’s a concrete API/edge-case concern rather than a verified break.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/assets/javascripts/discourse/routes/topic-unsubscribe.js.es6:6 — Client route `topicUnsubscribe` loads via `PostStream.loadTopicView` (`/t/:id.json` -> `topics#show`) and never calls the server `unsubscribe` endpoint, so client-side transitions to `/t/:slug/:id/unsubscribe` render the page without changing the notification level; only a full page load mutates state (client/server route mismatch).

adjudication.rationale: The Ember route `topic-unsubscribe.js.es6` defines `model(params)` that calls `PostStream.loadTopicView(params.id)` (i.e., loads the normal topic view JSON) and does not request the new Rails endpoint `topics#unsubscribe` added at `GET /t/:slug/:topic_id/unsubscribe` / `GET /t/:topic_id/unsubscribe`, where the notification_level mutation happens. Therefore, an in-app/client-side transition to `/t/:slug/:id/unsubscribe` would render the unsubscribe page without toggling notification state; only a full page load that hits `TopicsController#unsubscribe` would perform the change.

adjudication_records.issue_text: config/routes.rb:441 — GET t/:slug/:topic_id/unsubscribe` is a state-mutating GET; email link scanners/prefetchers and browser prefetch will silently mute topics, and it is cached/redirected with 301 like a read route.

adjudication.rationale: The diff introduces `TopicsController#unsubscribe`, which mutates per-user state by changing `TopicUser.notification_level` and calling `tu.save!` (topics_controller.rb). This action is wired up as a GET endpoint in `config/routes.rb` (`get "t/:slug/:topic_id/unsubscribe" => "topics#unsubscribe"` and `get "t/:topic_id/unsubscribe" => "topics#unsubscribe"`). Because it’s triggered via a simple GET link (also added into notification emails via `unsubscribe_url: post.topic.unsubscribe_url`), automated link scanners/prefetchers can unintentionally hit it and silently change a user’s notification state. Additionally, the action can issue a `301` redirect on slug mismatch (`redirect_to ... status: 301`), which is cacheable and can compound unintended behavior.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/controllers/topics_controller.rb:105 — TopicUser.find_by(...)` can return nil for users emailed via mention/quote without a topic_users row, producing NoMethodError (500) instead of a defined response.

If no `topic_users` row exists for that user/topic, `tu` will be `nil`, causing a `NoMethodError` and a 500. The diff shows no nil-handling (e.g., `TopicUser.change`/create or guard/404), so the finding is grounded in the added code path.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/controllers/topics_controller.rb:101 — Slug-mismatch redirect goes to the absolute `unsubscribe_url` with status 301 regardless of format, unlike `show` which redirects to a relative URL and preserves `.json`; JSON clients are permanently redirected to an HTML URL.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/controllers/topics_controller.rb:96 — The state mutation happens on an idempotency-free GET, so reloading the unsubscribe page (or a slug-corrected 301 followed twice) toggles again: watching -> regular -> muted on successive loads

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds `GET` routes to `topics#unsubscribe` (config/routes.rb) and implements `unsubscribe` to mutate `TopicUser.notification_level` (topics_controller.rb) by switching watching/tracking -> regular, otherwise -> muted. Because it’s a state-changing action on an idempotency-free GET, revisiting/reloading the unsubscribe URL can change the user’s notification state again (e.g., watching/tracking becomes regular on first load, then regular becomes muted on the next load). adjudication_records.issue_text: app/controllers/topics_controller.rb:107 — Toggle branches only on > regular, so a muted user re-clicking stays muted while a tracking/watching user is only dropped to regular (still gets reply/mention emails), which contradicts the "you will stop receiving notifications" copy and makes the link's effect depend on prior state

adjudication.rationale:
In the newly added `TopicsController#unsubscribe`, the toggle logic only mutes when `tu.notification_level` is `<= regular`; if it is `> regular` (e.g., tracking/watching), it is set to `regular` instead of `muted`:

```rb
if tu.notification_level > TopicUser.notification_levels[:regular]
  tu.notification_level = TopicUser.notification_levels[:regular]
else
  tu.notification_level = TopicUser.notification_levels[:muted]
end
```

This means users who were tracking/watching do not end up muted after using the “stop receiving notifications” unsubscribe link/copy, and muted users re-clicking remain muted (no toggle). The effect depends on prior state and contradicts the UI copy added in `client.en.yml` ("You will stop receiving notifications...").

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/controllers/topics_controller.rb:105 — TopicUser.find_by can return nil (any topic the user has no TopicUser row for, reachable by editing the id in the URL), causing NoMethodError/500 instead of a controlled response; use TopicUser.change or guard nil.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/controllers/topics_controller.rb:107 — Each hit degrades notification level (watching->regular->muted), so a link that is opened twice (or prefetched then clicked) mutes rather than unsubscribes; there is no idempotent/confirmation step protecting the user's intent.

This means repeated GETs to the same `/t/:id/unsubscribe` link will further change state (e.g., watching/tracking → regular on first hit, then regular → muted on second hit). Since the link is added to notification emails (`unsubscribe_url: post.topic.unsubscribe_url`) and can be opened multiple times (double-click, prefetch, link scanners), the behavior is not idempotent and can mute a topic unintentionally rather than just “stop receiving notifications” as the copy suggests.
